1.title: Access Management: Conditional Access and Roles
1.text: Welcome to Module five: Access Management: Conditional Access and Roles. It covers the exam area Capabilities of Microsoft Entra. Each part of this module comes from the study notes of the same name, so you can read the notes after you watch.

1.title: What You Will Learn
1.text: By the end of this module you will be able to do three things. Describe Microsoft Entra Conditional Access. Describe Microsoft Entra roles and role-based access control (R B A C). Practice with exam-style questions and a recall check.

1.title: Where This Fits in the Exam
1.text: Here is where this module sits in the exam. Exam area: Capabilities of Microsoft Entra (twenty-five to thirty percent). Exam format: forty-five minutes; a score of seven hundred on a scale of one to one thousand passes. Validated against: the official S C nine hundred study guide, skills measured as of October twenty-one, two thousand twenty-six.

1.title: Microsoft Entra Conditional Access
1.text: Microsoft Entra Conditional Access. Conditional Access is the policy engine of Zero Trust. It makes if-then decisions at sign-in: if certain signals are true, then apply a decision. User or group. Block access. Location (country or I P range). Grant access. Device (platform, compliant, managed). Grant but require M F A. Application being accessed. Require a compliant or hybrid-joined device. Sign-in risk and user risk (from I D Protection). Require an approved app, a password change or terms of use. Client app (browser, legacy protocols). Session controls, such as limited access or sign-in frequency.

1.title: Microsoft Entra Conditional Access, continued
1.text: Microsoft Entra Conditional Access. The figure shows this: Conditional Access: signals go in, a policy decides to block, require M F A or grant access.

1.title: Microsoft Entra Conditional Access, continued
1.text: Microsoft Entra Conditional Access. Key facts. Conditional Access needs Microsoft Entra I D P one or higher; risk-based conditions need P two. Policies can run in report-only mode to test the effect before enforcing them. Exclude emergency access (break-glass) accounts so an administrator cannot be locked out by mistake. Conditional Access is evaluated after the first factor (the user has signed in with the first method). Security defaults are the free alternative; they cannot be used together with Conditional Access policies.

1.title: Microsoft Entra Conditional Access, continued
1.text: Microsoft Entra Conditional Access. Typical policies: require M F A for all users, require M F A for administrators, block legacy authentication, require a compliant device for corporate apps, block sign-in from certain countries. Exam tip: "If the user is outside the office then require M F A" equals Conditional Access. It is identity-driven policy and it needs P one. Report-only mode tests a policy without enforcing it. Exam tip: Global Administrator can do everything, so keep very few and protect them with M F A. Other tasks need the narrowest role (least privilege).

1.title: Microsoft Entra roles
1.text: Microsoft Entra roles. Microsoft Entra roles (also called directory roles or administrator roles) give people the permissions to manage Microsoft Entra resources, such as users, groups and applications. Global Administrator. Everything in Entra I D and connected Microsoft services; use very few. User Administrator. Manage users and groups and reset passwords. Security Administrator. Manage security features and read security information. Global Reader. Read everything, change nothing. Conditional Access Administrator. Manage Conditional Access policies. Use the least-privilege principle: give people the narrowest role that lets them do their job, and keep the number of Global Administrators small (and protected with M F A).

1.title: Role-based access control (RBAC)
1.text: Role-based access control (R B A C). Role-based access control (R B A C) grants access by role instead of by person. A role assignment has three parts. Security principal. Who: a user, group, service principal or managed identity. Role definition. What: a collection of permissions. Scope. Where: the resource, resource group, subscription or management group.

1.title: Two role systems
1.text: Two role systems. Manages access to. Microsoft Entra roles: Microsoft Entra resources (users, groups, apps). Azure R B A C: Azure resources (V Ms, storage, networks). Scope. Microsoft Entra roles: Tenant, administrative unit, or an object. Azure R B A C: Management group, subscription, resource group, resource. Example roles. Microsoft Entra roles: Global Administrator, User Administrator. Azure R B A C: Owner, Contributor, Reader. Azure R B A C built-in roles: Owner (full access and can assign roles), Contributor (create and manage resources, cannot assign roles), Reader (view only).

1.title: Two role systems, continued
1.text: Two role systems. The figure shows this: Microsoft Entra roles manage identity resources; Azure R B A C manages Azure resources. Exam tip: Entra roles equals manage identities. Azure R B A C equals manage Azure resources. Owner can assign roles; Contributor cannot. Least privilege is the principle behind both. Assign roles to groups rather than individuals where possible.

1.title: Practice Question 1
1.text: Question one. Fabrikam Outdoors wants to require M F A only when a user signs in from outside the country. Which feature fits? The four options are on the screen. The answer is D: Conditional Access. Conditional Access applies if-then rules using signals such as location.

1.title: Practice Question 2
1.text: Question two. Before enforcing a new Conditional Access policy, the team wants to see its effect without blocking anyone. What should it use? The four options are on the screen. The answer is B: Report-only mode. Report-only mode evaluates a policy and logs the result without enforcing it.

1.title: Practice Question 3
1.text: Question three. Which role should be given to a person who only needs to reset user passwords? The four options are on the screen. The answer is A: User Administrator. Least privilege means the narrowest role that fits, such as User Administrator.

1.title: Practice Question 4
1.text: Question four. A user needs to create virtual machines in a resource group but must not assign roles to others. Which Azure R B A C role fits? The four options are on the screen. The answer is D: Contributor. Contributor can create and manage resources but cannot assign roles.

1.title: Practice Question 5
1.text: Question five. Which statement describes Microsoft Entra roles? The four options are on the screen. The answer is D: They give permissions to manage Microsoft Entra resources such as users and applications. Entra roles control administration of identity resources, while Azure R B A C controls Azure resources.

1.title: Practice Question 6
1.text: Question six. Which part of an R B A C role assignment states where the permissions apply? The four options are on the screen. The answer is D: Scope. The scope says where, such as a subscription or resource group.

1.title: Recall Check 1
1.text: Recall check one. Say each answer out loud before you listen to mine. Question one. What does Conditional Access do? Answer: Makes if-then access decisions at sign-in using signals. Question two. Which license level does Conditional Access need? Answer: Microsoft Entra I D P one or higher. Question three. Name three Conditional Access decisions. Answer: For example block, grant, require M F A, require a compliant device.

1.title: Recall Check 2
1.text: Recall check two. Say each answer out loud before you listen to mine. Question four. What are the three parts of a role assignment? Answer: Security principal, role definition and scope. Question five. Which Azure R B A C role can assign roles? Answer: Owner. Question six. Why exclude emergency access accounts from policies? Answer: So administrators cannot be locked out by a mistake.

1.title: Module Recap
1.text: Here is the recap. Conditional Access: if-then at sign-in; signals (user, location, device, app, risk). Entra roles: manage identity resources; Global Administrator (few), User Administrator, Security Administrator, Global Reader. R B A C: principal plus role definition plus scope; Azure roles Owner, Contributor, Reader; least privilege. Two systems: Entra roles equals identities; Azure R B A C equals Azure resources. In the next module, we continue the course.
